Paragraph: In Bhagavad Gita Chapter 17, Verses 15-16, Krishna describes true austerity of speech and mind: 'Words that are truthful, pleasant, beneficial, and non-agitating, along with regular recitation of sacred texts, constitute austerity of speech. Serenity of mind, gentleness, silence, self-restraint, and purity of purpose constitute austerity of the mind.'
Situation/Problem_Faced: Hurtful communication, internal mental chatter, verbal aggression, and emotional turmoil.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna details principles for mindful speech (Anudvega-kara) and mental discipline, advocating gentleness and calm reflection.
Outcome/Resolution: Practicing mindful speech and inner quiet reduces interpersonal conflict and promotes mental tranquility.

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Vang-maya Tapa (Austerity of speech: truth, sweetness, and benefit)
Manasa Tapa (Mental discipline: serenity and self-restraint)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Spiritual growth requires controlling one's speech and thoughts, ensuring interactions are truthful, kind, and peaceful.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Aligns with nonviolent communication (NVC) and cognitive self-regulation to improve relationships.
